findings_qualitative.value: Filamentary structures are ubiquitous in the 50MC, suggesting also in CMZ clouds

evidence.quote: The existence of a number of the filamentary structures in the 50MC strongly suggests that the filamentary structures are also ubiquitous in the molecular clouds in the CMZ.

claims.hypothesis: CCC compresses gas and increases dense bound cores
claims.experiment: Compare bound cores in R_T>2.5 CCC region vs non-CCC
claims.result: Similar bound core numbers in a ~14% area; higher densities in CCC; 26 cores >8.1e23 cm^-2 only in CCC
claims.finding: CCC compresses gas and increases number of dense bound cores

evidence.quote: The distributions indicate that the CCC compresses the molecular gas and increases the number of the dense bound cores.

claims.experiment: Power-law fits in CCC and non-CCC
claims.finding: Slope unchanged but massive cores form only in CCC

evidence.quote: We conclude that the slope of the CMF was not changed so much, but the compression by the CCC efficiently formed the massive bound H 13 CO + cores

claims.hypothesis: 50MC cores are more top-heavy than Orion A

evidence.quote: Therefore, the CMFs of the bound H 13 CO + in the 50MC have a top-heavy distribution compared with those in the Orion A

why_this_method.value: Bound cores defined as alpha<2 because abundance uncertainty of factor 2

evidence.quote: we consider the H 13 CO + core candidates with the virial parameters of less than 2 as ”bound cores”

limitations_admitted.value: Abundance uncertainty up to a factor of 2 affects masses

evidence.quote: Because the uncertainty of the abundance that is used to estimate the mass is up to a factor of 2

referee_caveats_inferred: Tex per core from a single LVG fit of C32S over a large region may be unreliable
Virial analysis ignores external pressure and magnetic fields
CMF fit has few bins and low dof
CCC region defined by R_T threshold chosen to cover masers; selection could bias comparisons
Virial parameters 10-100x Orion, so most candidates unbound; bound selection alpha<2 is abundance dependent
